parts.title: Multi-tasking and the brain
parts.article:
Multi-tasking and the brain
 
(A) Do you think you're a master of multi-tasking? Think again. Unless you are one of the three percent of super-taskers in the population, research shows that your brain isn't capable of paying close attention to more than one complex task at a time. Researchers who study attention say that effective multi-tasking is beyond most of us. Psychiatrist Edward M Hallowell even describes multi-tasking as 'a mythical activity in which people believe they can perform two or more tasks simultaneously as effectively as they can perform one'.
 
(B) It is true that you can check your email while eating your lunch, or listen to music while walking. But innate activities like walking, chewing, and breathing do not require you to pay attention, whereas activities such as reading, tapping out a text message, or driving a car do require attention. Why is paying attention to two things at once difficult? 'The brain can perform simultaneous tasks, but attention has capacity limitations,' says Associate Professor Paul E Dux, a cognitive neuroscientist at the University of Queensland in Australia. When you do only one thing at a time, you're better at that task than when you're doing multiple things concurrently. Take the classic multi-tasking scenario of talking on a mobile phone while driving - an ill-advised activity that many people believe they have mastered. When David Strayer, Professor of Psychology at the University of Utah in the US, and his team observed 56,000 drivers as they approached an intersection, the majority of drivers who were talking on their phone failed to stop in accordance with traffic laws. And it did not matter if the driver was using a handheld or hands-free device. Even with both eyes on the road and both hands on the wheel, drivers' performance was impaired. Strayer's research shows that performance deteriorates drastically when attention is split between tasks: more mistakes are made and it takes longer to complete each activity.
 
(C) The prefrontal cortex is the brain region responsible for choosing what to pay attention to, and for coordinating inputs from other brain areas. By scanning the prefrontal cortex of people while they multi-tasked, scientists at the French Institute of Health and Medical Research in Paris (INSERM) found that when people focused on a single thing, the right and left sides of the prefrontal cortex work together. But when people attempt to perform two things at once, the sides work independently. Neuroscientist Etienne Koechlin says his study demonstrates that while the brain can switch back and forth between two tasks, we might be in great trouble when we try to juggle more than two tasks, simply because we have only two frontal lobes'.
 
(D) To the question of whether there is a difference between the sexes, Koechlin's imaging studies uncovered no differences in the ability to switch between tasks in the prefrontal cortices of men or women. But other researchers studying real life scenarios such as finding lost keys, believe there might be some truth to the claim that women are superior multi-taskers. Women have a much better strategy for finding the keys, whereas men tend to jump to it and be far less organised and thorough. 'It's as if they don't stop to reflect and plan for a moment,' says Professor Keith Laws from the University of Hertfordshire in England. But while the ability to develop strategies for coping with the numerous tasks in everyday life could give women an advantage, 'nobody can juggle two, never mind three, "complex" tasks at the same time.'
 
(E) However, David Strayer's research uncovered that some rare people possess extraordinary multi-tasking ability. These so-called 'super-taskers' exhibit different patterns of brain activity when multi-tasking compared to ordinary people: they show less activity in the prefrontal cortex during multi-tasking, suggesting their brains are functioning with a high level of efficiency. Strayer thinks that pilots of high-performance aircraft, high-end chefs who can cook several meals at the same time to perfection, and elite doctors in hospital emergency rooms might all be more likely to be super-taskers. "All other things being equal, we suspect that super-taskers will rise to a top position in any occupation that places a high demand on juggling various tasks that demand attention at the same time.'
 
(F) The ability to multi-task probably comes down to the DNA you inherit from your parents to a large extent, says Strayer. 'You are either born with the neural structure that allows you to overcome the usual multi-tasking challenges, or you aren't. Super-taskers' brains are doing something we can't do.' All in all, these findings may have very real consequences on our lives.

analyses.content: 段落核心在否定普通人的多任务能力（beyond most of us / mythical），而非讨论性别或大脑结构。
(Section A) "Unless you are one of the three percent... research shows that your brain isn't capable of paying close attention to more than one complex task at a time."
A段指出除了极少数超级任务处理者外，大多数人的大脑无法同时关注多个复杂任务，甚至有专家称多任务处理是一种“神话（mythical activity）”，实际上几乎不可能做到，对应选项 iv（真正的多任务处理几乎是不可能的）。
B段区分了本能活动（innate activities，如走路）不需要注意力，而阅读、开车等活动需要注意力，解释了为什么有时能做两件事有时不能，对应选项 iii（区分人们能和不能进行多任务处理的情况）。
段落开头就在做对比（innate vs require attention），这就是“Distinction（区别）”。
(Section B) "But innate activities... do not require you to pay attention, whereas activities such as reading... do require attention."
C段从神经科学角度（prefrontal cortex, frontal lobes）解释了为什么我们难以处理两个以上的任务——因为我们只有两个额叶，对应选项 vi（难以管理更多事情的神经学原因）。
关键词“reasons for struggling”对应原文的“great trouble”，“neurological”对应原文的“brain region / frontal lobes”。不要选ii，因为ii强调的是“影响（effects）”，而本段讲的是“原因（because we have only two frontal lobes）”。
(Section C) "...we might be in great trouble when we try to juggle more than two tasks, simply because we have only two frontal lobes'."
虽然开头提到了大脑皮层（neurological structure），但整段都在围绕“difference between the sexes”展开讨论。
D段主要讨论了关于“性别（sexes / men or women）”差异的研究和观点，涉及男性女性在多任务处理上的表现对比，对应选项 v（多任务处理与性别）。
(Section D) "To the question of whether there is a difference between the sexes... women are superior multi-taskers."
E段列举了飞行员、顶级厨师和急诊室医生等职业，认为这些领域可能存在超级任务处理者，对应选项 i（可能会发现超级任务处理者的职业）。
“Professions”对应原文列举的“pilots, chefs, doctors”。
(Section E) "Strayer thinks that pilots... high-end chefs... and elite doctors... might all be more likely to be super-taskers."
F段指出多任务处理能力很大程度上取决于你从父母那里继承的DNA，即基因决定，对应选项 vii（多任务处理能力由基因决定）。
“Determined by people's genes” 对应原文的 “comes down to the DNA you inherit”。
(Section F) "The ability to multi-task probably comes down to the DNA you inherit from your parents..."

questions.question: The brain of a good multi-tasker works differently from other people’s.

analyses.content: (Section E) "These so-called 'super-taskers' exhibit different patterns of brain activity... says Strayer."
“Works differently” 对应 “different patterns of brain activity”。
题目说优秀的多任务处理者的大脑运作方式与常人不同。E段 David Strayer 的研究发现“super-taskers（超级任务者）”表现出“different patterns of brain activity（不同的大脑活动模式）”，选 C。

questions.question: The rate of error is considerably higher when people multi-task.

analyses.content: 题目说多任务处理时错误率相当高。B段 David Strayer 的研究表明，当注意力分散时，“performance deteriorates drastically... more mistakes are made（表现急剧恶化，犯更多错）”，选 C。
“Rate of error is higher” 对应 “more mistakes are made”。
(Section B) "Strayer's research shows that... more mistakes are made..."

questions.question: People are mistaken in their assumption that they can multi-task.

analyses.content: 题目说人们误以为自己可以多任务处理。A段 Edward M Hallowell 描述多任务处理是一种“mythical activity（神话般的活动）”，人们“believe they can perform...（相信他们能做）”但实际上做不到，选 A。
“Mistaken in their assumption” 对应原文的 “mythical activity / believe they can...”。
(Section A) "Psychiatrist Edward M Hallowell even describes multi-tasking as 'a mythical activity in which people believe they can perform...'"

questions.question: One gender does not seem to pause to consider before taking action.

analyses.content: (Section D) "'It's as if they don't stop to reflect and plan for a moment,' says Professor Keith Laws..."
题目说某一种性别似乎在行动前不稍作停顿思考。D段 Keith Laws 说男性倾向于直接行动（jump to it），“It's as if they don't stop to reflect and plan for a moment（好像他们不会停下来反思和计划片刻）”，选 E。
“One gender” 指 “men”，“does not seem to pause to consider” 对应 “don't stop to reflect”。

groups.contentHtml:
Super-taskers
Super-taskers are those of us who possess special multi-tasking ability. They can be found in all professions. People who are pilots, chefs and doctors are often super-taskers, and super-taskers are most likely to achieve a that is high on the career ladder.
Super-taskers typically have to undertake many tasks simultaneously that need their .
Genes play an important role in having this capability: these people have a special brain , which helps them do what we cannot.

“Achieve a ... high on the career ladder” 是原文 “rise to a top position” 的同义改写。
(Section E) "...we suspect that super-taskers will rise to a top position in any occupation..."

“Need” 对应原文的 “demand”。
(Section E) "...juggling various tasks that demand attention at the same time."
